subject: Post-call: MedicoHealth buying playbook, latency & cost clarity
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Turner <elaine.turner@medicohealth.com>, James Holt <james.holt@medicohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-12T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — MedicoHealth inference priorities

Hi Elaine / James —

Thanks again for the time today. Short recap from our side and three asks to keep momentum: 

What we heard (confirm / correct):
- Key use case: clinical search + short summarization for provider notes (typical prompt <= 128 tokens).
- Primary decision criteria: latency, predictable cost, and security controls (VPC/KMS).
- Preferred deployment: VPC/private deployment, but open to Redwood Dedicated if separation + SLA are achievable.
- Stakeholders you flagged: Elaine (econ buyer / product lead), James (procurement), Sunil (security/compliance).

Latency / cost targets mentioned on call (please confirm):
- Latency: P95 <= 150ms for <=128-token generation in typical baseline traffic (burst to 200 qps).
- Cost: target of roughly <$0.01 per request (equivalently ~<$0.0008/token depending on payload) to hit economics for product rollout.

Immediate asks (next week):
1) Elaine / James: confirm procurement timeline and any mandatory procurement docs (PO cadence, vendor packet).
2) Sunil / security: we’ll send an RFI/SOC2 answers doc — please flag any additional evidence you need.
3) Redwood internal: run an initial latency/cost feasibility run on our side and share a short benchmark plan.

Attachments: I’ve attached a draft RFI answer set and a proposed benchmark CSV that lists payload shapes we’d run.

Next steps I propose from Redwood:
- Deliver a 2-day benchmark plan (non-prod) that runs closest-match model variants and measures P50/P95/P99 for the 128-token and 512-token profiles.
- Share an SLA summary for Dedicated and Hosted VPC options, including uptime, incident response, and data controls.
- Draft a mutual action plan with milestones toward procurement/PO.

Can you confirm stakeholders and the timeline (commercial committee / procurement windows) so we can align resources?

Thanks —
Rishi
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: Medico_RFI_Security_Answers.pdf (PDF, 12 pages)
Attachment: medico_benchmark_requirements.csv (CSV, 1 KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-12T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — MedicoHealth inference priorities

Thanks Rishi — good capture. A few operational notes from GTM/solutions: 

1) Benchmark approach: Karthik, can you own a 48-hour non-prod run that exercises the following payloads from the attached CSV? We'll report P50/P95/P99 and cost per 1K tokens. Target to produce the first draft by Thu 6/17.
   - profile A: 0-128 tokens, 70% of traffic
   - profile B: 129-512 tokens, 25% of traffic
   - profile C: >512 tokens (edge), 5%

2) Deployment recommendation: start with Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) to guarantee baseline throughput and then propose a VPC option for longer-term control if Medico wants KMS + private peering. Marissa to draft a comparison sheet (Dedicated vs VPC) for Elaine.

3) Commercial / timelines: Connors, can you prepare an anchor quote for a 12-month reserved commitment and a lighter 'proof-of-value' month to month option? We should have that by 6/18.

I'll also prepare a short one-pager describing the SLA buckets (latency SLOs vs uptime vs support response).

-Marissa
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Elaine Turner <elaine.turner@medicohealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: James Holt <james.holt@medicohealth.com>, Dr. Sunil Rao <sunil.rao@medicohealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-13T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — MedicoHealth inference priorities

Rishi / Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming a few points from our end: 

- Stakeholders: Yes — I’m the product/econ owner and will drive the business case. James (procurement) will lead vendor intake. Sunil will lead security evaluation. I'll loop in Legal after procurement flags the vendor packet.
- Procurement timeline: We have a purchasing window the week of 7/12 (committee reviews). Ideally we need pricing and basic SLA language by 6/28 to review internally.
- Deployment preference: We prefer VPC-first (data residency + KMS). If Redwood Dedicated provides equivalent isolation and a committable SLA, that is acceptable — but Sunil will need the SOC2 and encryption-at-rest details.

Questions for you: 
1) Can Redwood provide a concise SLA example (uptime %, credit language, response times for Sev1/Sev2) for both Dedicated and VPC?
2) Do you have public benchmark numbers for P95 on 128-token workloads on your Dedicated offering? If not, we accept a short PoV but would prioritize vendors who can show baseline numbers.

We’ll also email our standard vendor packet to James and will need a PO-to-contract cadence.

Thanks — looking forward to the benchmark plan.

Elaine
VP Product, MedicoHealth
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Turner <elaine.turner@medicohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-13T14:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — MedicoHealth inference priorities

Elaine — excellent, thanks for the clarity. Action items and answers below: 

Answers: 
- SLA summary: Attached is a one-page SLA extract for Dedicated and VPC (high-level): uptime target 99.9% monthly (with credit schedule), Sev1 response within 1 hour, Sev2 within 4 hours. We’ll tailor language if legal wants changes.
- Benchmarks: Public baseline (internal): for our Dedicated pool running a 70B-class model surrogate tuned for small prompts we typically see P95 ~ 120-160ms at steady-state at the 0-128 token profile depending on batching. We'll run your exact payloads in non-prod and deliver concrete numbers.

Planned timeline (Redwood):
- 6/14: Karthik to start non-prod benchmark (48h).
- 6/17: Internal benchmark report + cost estimates (per 1K tokens and per-request).
- 6/18: Commercial anchor quotes (Connor).
- 6/21: Deliver draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) + security RFI answers (attached).

Attachments: Medico_RFI_Security_Answers.pdf (answers + SOC2 pointer). Benchmark CSV is the measurements we propose to run.

Related links: https://hubspot.example.com/deals/20345 (hubspot deal), https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-Medico-MAP (MAP draft).

If that timeline works, I’ll schedule a short 30-minute kickoff for the benchmark and loop Sunil for any test-data constraints (we’ll use synthetic data keyed to your shapes).

Best,
Rishi
From: Elaine Turner <elaine.turner@medicohealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: James Holt <james.holt@medicohealth.com>, Dr. Sunil Rao <sunil.rao@medicohealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-14T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — MedicoHealth inference priorities

Thanks — timeline looks good. Please go ahead with the benchmark kickoff 6/14 and loop Sunil on synthetic data constraints. James, please share the vendor packet when you have it and we'll aim to review SLA language by 6/28.

Elaine
